statements.text: There is likely a berserk wing of the artificial intelligence community that intentionally or unintentionally could use artificial intelligence to kill all of us and hurt us the entire time that we are dying.
statements.context: Senator Kennedy poses a question to a witness during a Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI oversight.

statements.text: We ought to first pass a law that says you can use AI for these uses but not others. Is that what you're saying?
statements.context: Senate hearing on AI oversight, Senator Kennedy questioning a witness about whether AI use cases should be restricted by law.

statements.text: And so I would have funding to try to basically focus on AI safety research. That term has a lot of complications in my field.
statements.context: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI rules where Senator Kennedy questions witness Professor Gary Marcus.

statements.text: Sensible safeguards are not in opposition to innovation. Accountability is not a burden. Far from it. They are the foundation of how we can move ahead while protecting public trust.
statements.context: Opening statement by Senator Blumenthal at a Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI oversight.

statements.text: Yes. Mr. Dally, if I am a recipient of content created by generative AI, do you think I should have a right to know that that content was generated by a robot?
statements.context: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI oversight; Senator Kennedy questions witness Bill Dally (NVIDIA Chief Scientist) about consumer transparency for AI-generated content.

statements.text: It says if you own a robot that's going to spit out artificial content to consumers, consumers have the right to know that it was generated by a robot and who owns the robot.
statements.context: Senate Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI oversight where Senator Kennedy reflects on legislative readiness and describes his disclosure bill.

statements.text: But as a principle, do you think that people should have a right to know when they're being fed content from generative AI?
statements.context: Senate hearing titled 'Oversight of A.I.: Legislating on Artificial Intelligence', with Senator Kennedy questioning a witness.

statements.text: In terms of do we have some sort of overarching regulatory framework that we’re close to agreeing on that addresses the dangers and potential of artificial intelligence, in my judgment no. We just don’t right now.
statements.venue: Remarks to reporters after Senate AI forum with tech executives

statements.text: Professor, do you think the consumer should be able to know not only that the content is generated by AI, but do you think this consumer is entitled to know who owns the robot and therefore the generated content?
statements.context: Senate hearing on Artificial Intelligence in Financial Services, where Senator Kennedy questions an expert witness.

statements.text: Do you think AI can improve on that in terms of determining precisely who is likely to pay the loan back and who is not?
statements.context: Senate hearing on Artificial Intelligence in Financial Services, questioning a witness about AI in loan underwriting.

statements.text:
AI is moving quickly, and so are the scammers who are using it to exploit unsuspecting Americans.

Our bill would tell consumers whether what they’re reading, seeing or hearing is the product of AI, and that’s clarity that people desperately need.

https://t.co/PlNnx7gPCX

Our bill would set an AI-based standard to protect U.S. consumers by telling them whether what they're reading, seeing or hearing is the product of AI, and that's clarity that people desperately need.
statements.venue: Press statement on AI Labeling Act

statements.text:
AI is relatively new, so existing law isn’t sufficient.

AI will make our lives better if it doesn’t kill us first, so our bill would start managing the AI threat by stopping people from using AI to commit financial fraud. https://t.co/v6fct1cdQp

AI is moving quickly, and our laws must prevent AI manipulation from rattling our financial markets.

I’m working with @MarkWarner to help ensure that AI threats don't put Americans’ investments and retirement dreams at risk.

https://t.co/gyTpKKPWsD

As a matter of fact, just last week a report from the Department of Homeland Security warned, and I will quote, ``As the 2024 election cycle progresses, generative AI tools likely provide both domestic and foreign threat actors with enhanced opportunities for interference by aggravating emergent events, disrupting election processes, or attacking election infrastructure.''
statements.context: House Homeland Security Committee hearing on AI and homeland defense, held during the 2024 election cycle.

statements.text: But how can we better harness the institutes of higher ed, especially our public institutions, for getting at this cutting-edge technology? While they are training up our youth in this new technology how do we make sure that they are developing it in a safe way regarding AI?
statements.context: House Homeland Security Committee hearing on harnessing AI to secure the homeland.

statements.text: You don't know whether the advanced Nvidia artificial intelligence chips are prohibited from being sold to China?
statements.context: Senate hearing on national security through export controls, investment security, and the Defense Production Act.

Friends, I guess in 2025 you have to do this sort of thing…but please ignore the AI-generated fake news stories you may have seen about my family and me these past few days on social media claiming we experienced tragedy.

We are all healthy, happy, safe, and sound! We are working with Facebook to remove all of the fake stories.

I hope you and your family have a wonderful Sunday and a happy Thanksgiving!
Here’s my worry: that a lot of this stuff about artificial intelligence making us more productive is a bunch of hype by people who want to sell stock. I’d be careful there.

statements.text: The people who have developed AI are very, very smart. But they’re high IQ stupid people. You might let them tutor you. But you wouldn’t want them to date your sister. They’re terrible marketers.

First, they’re going to have to stop using so much water. Go to a closed-loop system. Number two, they’re going to have to provide their own energy. Number three, they’re going to have to devise buildings that are slightly aesthetic.
The American people look at it. They’re not stupid. They get it. They think, “Well, AI could make our lives better if it doesn’t take our jobs and kill us all first.”

AI can make our lives better—but not if data centers waste our water, increase our electricity bills and take our tax dollars. Use less water. Provide your own energy.

Stop demanding taxpayer subsidies.

Level with the American people about what AI means. https://t.co/0bIDsq4ZuA

Here is the risk: AI is supposed to be a tool that human beings have control of to make our lives better. But what happens if the AI model, through what’s called recursive self-improvement, which basically means it’s learning on its own, no longer becomes a tool; it becomes an independent species, separate and apart from human beings that we can’t control because it’s an independent species? And it doesn’t share our values. It doesn’t share human values.
statements.venue: Senate floor speech on AI Emergency Button Act (press release)

statements.text: In my mind, if there is even a 1% chance that one of these AI models can shed its nature as a tool and become an independent species and start doing whatever the hell it wants to do, if there’s even a 1% chance, we ought to take it seriously.
statements.venue: Senate floor speech on AI Emergency Button Act (press release)

statements.text: So, what do we do about it? Well, I’ve got a bill, and it basically says that if you’re going to sell an advanced AI model in the United States of America, it has got to have a kill switch. It doesn’t put the federal government, or any government, in charge of the kill switch. It puts the companies who own the model in charge of the kill switch.
statements.venue: Senate floor speech on AI Emergency Button Act (press release)

statements.text: It just says the AI companies have to have a fire extinguisher. They decide when to use it, but they've got to have one.
statements.venue: Senate floor remarks reported by USA Today

statements.text:
If AI models start acting like the Terminator, we need a way to shut them down.

I introduced a bill that requires AI models to have a kill switch.
 
The AI guys say they’re worried about what their models could do. They ought to do something about it.

AI is supposed to be a tool that humans control—not the other way around.

Advanced AI models need a kill switch in case they go off the rails. We don’t need another government-run committee to tell us that. https://t.co/aXyvc6ex8b
“But how is it going to impede the development of AI if we do something to gain the confidence of the American people in AI?”
